newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-HILL FAILS TO START GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL FAILS TO START GRAND PRIX.

text.p: World drivers champion Damon Hill endured a miserable start to his title defence when he failed to start the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on Sunday after his Arrows car broke down during a warm-up lap.
The 36-year-old Briton learned the realities of his new status as number one driver with one of Formula One's struggling teams when his car failed to reach the starting grid at Albert Park.
Hill, who won in Melbourne last year to launch his successful campaign, was unceremoniously discarded by the Williams team mid-way through last season.
He scraped into the race on Sunday by finishing 20th fastest in qualifying after the Arrows was beset with gearbox problems.
Hill, who limited his ambitions to completing the 58-lap race, stepped out of his car as soon as it came to a stop.
